title: perf-bench-scratchpad - latency & throughput runs (A100 / H100)
content:
Goal:
- quick scratchpad for recent latency/throughput runs (13B-ish models) across A100 and H100. capture configs, raw numbers, rough charts refs, and next steps.

Summary / TL;DR:
- H100 shows ~1.4x lower median latency and ~1.6x higher tokens/s vs A100 for q4 runs on this model (13B variant). p95 improvement is larger when streaming disabled.
- KV-cache massively improves throughput for repeated-prefix workloads (x3 tokens/s vs cold-start).
- Batching helps throughput linearly up to batch 8; tail latency (p95) jumps after batch >=16.

Experimental setup (notes):
- model: llama2-13b (open variant) and small internal 13B-optimized fork (same config for runs).
- quant: q4_o2 (bitsandbytes q4-like), also tried int8 on H100 for a couple runs.
- hardware: AWS p4d (A100 40GB) and p5d (H100) boxes; single-GPU experiments only here.
- infra: Redwood runtime dev branch: perf/reg-batching v0.9 (local build), request path uses continuous batching disabled for single-stream runs unless noted.
- prompt profile: prompt_len=32 tokens, gen_len=128 tokens. measured end-to-end request latency (client -> runtime -> model -> client) and tokens/sec = total_gen_tokens / total_elapsed_seconds over steady-state window.
- kv-cache tests: warm vs cold runs (warm = repeated prompt prefix cached in memory, cold = fresh generation).

Raw runs (selected):
1) A100, q4_o2, batch=1, no kv-cache, streaming=on
   - p50: 95 ms (per request), p95: 310 ms
   - gen_tokens=128, measured tokens/s ~= 1340
   - notes: decent median, tail high and flaky due to kernel launch jitter + memcpy spikes.

2) H100, q4_o2, batch=1, no kv-cache, streaming=on
   - p50: 68 ms, p95: 170 ms
   - tokens/s ~= 2150
   - notes: much smoother tail, lower variance. int8 run on H100 gave similar median but occasional regressions (investigate kernel selection).

3) A100, q4_o2, batch=8, no kv-cache, streaming=off
   - throughput (aggregate tokens/s): ~9800 tokens/s (per-GPU), per-request p50 ~220 ms, p95 ~560 ms
   - notes: batching increases aggregate throughput ~7.3x vs batch=1 but per-request latency increases. good for async bulk workloads.

4) H100, q4_o2, batch=8, no kv-cache, streaming=off
   - throughput ~16000 tokens/s, p50 ~150 ms, p95 ~310 ms
   - notes: H100 better scaling with batch due to tensor cores and larger sustained memory BW.

5) A100, q4_o2, batch=1, kv-cache warm (prefix cached), streaming=on
   - p50: 40 ms, p95: 90 ms, tokens/s ~= 3800
   - notes: prefix caching reduces compute by avoiding re-encoding prefix; shows x2.8-3x tokens/s improvement for repeated-prefix traffic (chat-like workloads).

6) H100, q4_o2, batch=1, kv-cache warm, streaming=on
   - p50: 28 ms, p95: 60 ms, tokens/s ~= 5600

7) Stress test (A100 x1), sustained concurrent qps ramp (batching auto-collect):
   - at target qps/throughput where batching aggregated to ~batch 12-16, observed p95 explosion (>900 ms) and occasional OOMs on regen peaks. Need to tune batch cutoffs and memory accounting.

Observations / quick conclusions:
- H100 is consistently faster and more stable for these 13B q4 runs. for latency-sensitive single-request workloads, H100 preferred (cost caveat).
- Kv-cache is one of the highest leverage optimizations for chat/assistant workloads. recommend default enable for pinned sessions.
- Batching is effective for throughput but must be tuned; large batches (>12) hurt tail latency and increase memory pressure. autoscaler should avoid reaching those batch sizes for latency-SLO customers.
- Streaming reduces observed p95 slightly (because partial tokens returned) but doesn't change total compute; careful when comparing end-to-end metrics vs non-streaming runs.
- int8 on H100 occasionally regresses; likely kernel fallback path. file a follow-up to trace kernel selection for int8 paths.

Open questions / next steps:
- rerun with model variants: 7B / 13B / 70B-ish trimmed variants to create cost/latency curves (needed for pricing recommendations).
- re-run same experiments with Redwood runtime v1.0-beta (optimizations: fused-attention, improved memcpy) to quantify improvements.
- add mixed-batch traffic pattern tests (mix of short prompts and long prompts) to validate batching heuristics.
- dig into int8 kernel selection on H100 (linked to confluence/INF-2342).
- produce graphs from raw logs and drop into sheet: sheet:1A2b3C_performance_runs (linked).

Quick commands (where I ran):
- run single: ./bench_client --host dev-redwood:8080 --model llama2-13b --quant q4_o2 --batch 1 --prompt-len 32 --gen 128 --streaming true
- run batch: ./bench_client --batch 8 --streaming false --samples 200
- kv warm test: run 10 warm requests with same prefix, then 200 measured requests

Notes to self:
- attach perf traces (nvprof / nsys) for one A100 and one H100 run and upload to s3 path above.
- compare costs: H100 raw hourly cost higher; compute tokens/s per $ to get cost-effectiveness metric.
- remember to exclude initialization / model-load time from steady-state numbers (we did for these runs).

References / artifacts:
- raw logs: s3://redwood-perf/logs/2025-11-15-ethan-wang (linked)
- sheet: sheet:1A2b3C_performance_runs (contains charts + aggregated p50/p95)
- confluence writeup: confluence:INFR-2342-model-onboarding (draft)

End.
